- When sentiment is consistently low (0.00–0.33) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for near-term (1–7d) horizon.
- After a sharp spike in sentiment (e.g., 1.00), model often overreacts with exaggerated highs; cap forecast at 1.5x recent peak or 20% above prior 7d average.
- If sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), model frequently underestimates downward moves; add 5–15% buffer for 10–30d horizon.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >2.5x recent 7d average, adjust down to 1.5x average or 1.2x prior 14d high.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome is >1.5x forecast, model likely missed a downward trend; apply “sentiment decay” rule: reduce forecast by 10–30% if sentiment was >0.67 in last 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00/0.33, model tends to underestimate lows; add 5–10% to forecast for 1–7d horizon to capture “sentiment lag” effect.
